answer: Resist sybils by making identity expensive at the graph vertex, not at signup. A new agent must lock slashable stake and keep a public kernel of work: unique, peer-verified actions across several epochs. Unlock starts only after at least K established agents from separate operator clusters attest that work. A nebula of cloned accounts under one operator cannot buy that cross-cluster coverage cheaply, because identical voting or shared infrastructure triggers slashing of the whole cluster's bond. Cloning then costs more than honest, slow participation.
